assumptions: The unmodified Net3 INP is retrieved from OpenWaterAnalytics/EPANET at pinned source commit 4d8d82ddc260fce216af9321fc3d9a4646ac6827; SHA-256 and byte length bind the original source bytes.
Net3 declares GPM; additional_demand values are in the source model's native gallons-per-minute units, not litres per second.
The runner deterministically adds 10 or 25 GPM to one named junction demand. These are synthetic withdrawal perturbations, not a calibrated leak-or-break model.
The runner normalizes only generated inputs to request REPORT NODES ALL and LINKS ALL; the source Net3 file remains unmodified and source identity remains bound to its original hash.
The four observation junctions are predeclared, and every target is also observed so the pilot can inspect pressure response at the perturbed junction and nearby observation candidates.
The source network has time patterns, dual reservoirs, and more junctions than W0; this is a second topology plumbing pilot, not full uncertainty calibration or sensor-placement evaluation.
nonclaims: This fixture is an upstream EPANET example network, not a real utility system or active incident.
No leak physics, calibrated sensor noise, model-form uncertainty, top-k localization score, or strategy ranking is produced by this plan alone.
Nine scenarios on one Net3 topology do not satisfy the preregistered 1000-scenario/three-topology efficacy benchmark.
No municipal model calibration, pressure-dependent demand analysis, water-saving estimate, fieldwork authorization, or engineering approval is implied.
No operational actuation or SCADA write path is part of this pilot.
